## 2. Prior Knowledge

**Literature mode**: {`none` | `allowed` | `blind`: copied from the run's `literature_mode` and shown at Approval (section 11), where it may be changed; when the run has no such field, proposed by the agent and confirmed by the human at Approval; never assumed. `none`: no literature is searched and no LITERATURE is produced; materials a human attached in the run's `literature` field remain allowed, marked `given` in the paragraph below, and are the only literature this PLAN may cite. `allowed`: besides the attached materials, literature enters this PLAN only through LITERATURE artifacts. `blind`: as `allowed`, plus the Excluded table: its items must not be retrieved or cited because they could reveal the answer; attached materials are checked against the Excluded table by the human at Approval (the gate does not see them).}

**Excluded**: {Under `none` and `allowed` write `none` after the label and delete the table. {Literature or materials attached to the run (its `literature` field), each marked `given`, or `No additional materials`. Knowledge-base pages and memory entries injected into phase context, each marked `given`, `recalled (<page or memory id>)`, or `assumed`. A claim from a LITERATURE cites it as `<LITERATURE ID>, claim n`, where claim n is the n-th data row of that LITERATURE's Claims table, counted from 1 in table order; a paper neither attached to the run nor in a LITERATURE Set is not cited. A claim may enter section 8 or license a parameter range only as `verified`: quote and location in the source checked on this run. ## 7. Experiment Design Policy

{New points are designed, not guessed. Prefer the design tool available to the agent (Fisher-optimality proposal with the current model and estimates); a manual design states why the tool was not used. Every proposed point carries exactly one primary justification from the table below, stated before the call. A point that cannot be assigned one is not run.}

| Justification | What must be stated for each point | Typical method |
|---------------|------------------------------------|----------------|
| Variance reduction | which output(s) (parameter, estimate, decision margin) it tightens and the expected gain | design tool with current model and estimates ({criterion}) |
| Information / discrimination | which open pair of the latest COMPARISON it separates, which hypothesis IDs differ between its members, and how different their predictions are at this point | design tool over competing models, or a manual discriminating design |
| Boundary of applicability | which assumption or condition range is being pushed and what the current law predicts there | manual, at or beyond the edge of the explored condition ranges |

{Rules for this run: when the design tool is mandatory, when manual points are allowed, how many boundary points per cycle, and what happens when a proposed point duplicates an existing one within noise.}

## 8. Hypothesis Space

{The starting candidate (model, hypothesis encoding, or procedure) is the simplest one that can answer the question: name it, count its free parameters, and state the conditions under which it is claimed to hold. Every further hypothesis is an addition to it: say how many parameters it adds, where it is claimed to apply, and the condition under which it would change the observable. Each starts as NOT YET TESTED. Discrimination points in section 7 are justified by rows of this table. (For enzyme kinetics this was product inhibition, substrate inhibition, cooperativity, binding order, thermal denaturation, ping-pong vs ternary complex.)}

Starting candidate: {name}, {k} free parameters, claimed applicable for {condition ranges}.

**ID**: `cpt-{system}-hypothesis-{slug}`

**Mechanism or effect**: {…}
**Parameters added**: {n}

**Status**: NOT YET TESTED
**Diagnostic condition**: {…}

{Status vocabulary: `NOT YET TESTED`; `SUPPORTED (batch <id>, RUN <id>)`; `FALSIFIED (batch <id>, RUN <id>)`. Status changes come only from section 7 of a COMPARISON; this list is the register, the COMPARISON is the evidence. One block per hypothesis, each defined by its `**ID**:` line so that DATASET, RUN and COMPARISON can reference it. A FALSIFIED row is not re-proposed without new data that the falsifying batch did not contain.}

{Selection rule for this run. Equal quality means: difference on the agreed quality metric (section 9) ≤ {…} between two candidates run on the same snapshot, or {information criterion} difference ≤ {…}. Among candidates of equal quality the one with fewer free parameters is selected. A parameter stays in the candidate only if removing it breaks equality. An applicability claim may not extend beyond the explored condition ranges in the DATASET. With more than two candidates, comparison is pairwise on the same snapshot, criterion by criterion, and is recorded in one COMPARISON per snapshot per phase: a candidate that loses or ties every criterion against another is dropped, the non-dominated ones are the open pairs the next discrimination batch must separate. No composite score: criteria are never weighted into one number, and a ranking never substitutes for a discriminating batch.}

## 9. Verdict Criteria

{The metric is agreed with a human, not chosen by the agent. Rows `units-match`, `budget`, `parsimony`, `applicability`, `checklist` are process criteria that hold for any procedure; the quality metric itself and any procedure-specific criterion are placeholders until the human fills them. Every criterion is either `given` by the human or `proposed` by the agent with a justification: what the quantity measures, why it answers section 1, and what it would miss. Each carries the name and date of the human who confirmed it. The table is frozen when the first phase starts: no row added, removed, or re-thresholded afterwards. A change of metric is a new PLAN with a new ID; RUNs judged under the old PLAN are not re-scored. Criteria are listed in the order they are evaluated: mechanical gates first, judged criteria last. A judged criterion names the human who judges or a judge with a CALIBRATION reference; without either it fails closed. The verdict is the vector of criteria; there is no composite score. One block per criterion, each defined by its `**ID**:` line; a RUN or COMPARISON that cites a criterion not defined here fails `cfs validate`.}

Frozen at: {date, before phase 1}. Confirmed by: {person}.

**ID**: `cpt-{system}-criterion-units-match`

**Direction**: ==

## 10. Stop Conditions

{When the run stops early: simulate or real budget exhausted; every checklist row TESTED and the best RUN on ground truth passes all criteria; the user stops the run; a tool failure fails the phase rather than being retried silently; actual simulation time exceeds the confirmed cost by {factor}; the human changes the metric, which closes this PLAN and opens a new one. Budget left over is not a reason to stop early, and fewer experiments is never one: while the latest COMPARISON has an `open` pair and budget remains, the run continues with the batch that separates it. A final result is presented only after `{result_gate}` PASS (COMPARISON rules 8, 9).}
